title: Offline Upgrade Validation Harness and Simulated Workload Suite
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Summary:

This page describes the offline upgrade validation harness and simulated workload suite used to validate private deployments before field upgrades or model swaps. The harness lets operators perform deterministic, repeatable validations of control-plane changes, runtime binary upgrades, model quantization swaps, and KV-cache migrations without impacting production tenants. It encodes a set of workload profiles, failure injection scenarios, telemetry assertions, and acceptance criteria required for sign-off.

Goals and scope:

- Provide an automated, reproducible validation path for upgrades that cannot be fully exercised in production canaries (air-gapped QA).
- Validate performance regressions (p50/p95/p99), correctness of model outputs for a set of golden prompts, and KV-cache consistency during stateful migrations.
- Exercise network/egress/fallback policies, tenant isolation rules, and KMS/HSM integrations in a safe sandbox.
- Produce an evidence bundle (logs, traces, metrics, artifacts) suitable for compliance audits and customer acceptance tests (CATs).

Out of scope:

- Non-deterministic A/B experimentation across live traffic.
- Long-term capacity soak tests longer than 72 hours (these are executed in separate stress labs).

Audience:

This document is intended for:
- Operators and SREs responsible for private deployment upgrades.
- Field engineers executing customer upgrades and runbook authors.
- Release engineers validating binary and package images.

High-level architecture of the harness:

1) Controller: a containerized orchestration component that coordinates profile playback, failure injection, and artifact collection.
2) Workload generator: pluggable modules that emulate request patterns for text generation, chat, embeddings, and KV-access at configurable QPS and token distributions.
3) Failure injector: network latency/jitter, process restarts, OOM simulation, GPU thermal spikes (simulated via throttling), and KMS latency stubs.
4) Telemetry validator: a rules engine that consumes traces/metrics/logs and evaluates pass/fail assertions.
5) Evidence bundler: packages logs, trace snapshots, diffs of golden outputs, and a human-friendly summary for sign-off.

Prerequisites and environment:

- Offline validation cluster that mirrors customer topology (minimum: 3 control-plane nodes, 6 worker nodes with representative GPU types).
- Ingested model artifacts: both current and candidate model binaries / quantized variants.
- Sample tenant configs and KV snapshots exported from production (sanitized).
- Network replay facility or traffic generator with TLS termination mirroring customer certs.
- Secrets: test KMS keys or HSM simulator. Ensure keys are marked test and are not customer secrets.

Workload profiles (bundled):

Each profile is a YAML file included in the suite. Profiles represent realistic mixes of requests and token distributions. Representative profiles: 

- small-text-search (embeddings-heavy): 100 QPS, 90% 128-token prompts, 10% 512-token prompts, embeddings batch size 32.
- conversational-saas (chat-heavy): 40 QPS, average 6 messages/session, 30% streaming responses, 15% function-calls.
- bursty-webhook (burst patterns): base 5 QPS with bursts to 800 QPS for 30s every 10m (tests autoscaling and burst policies).
- large-gen (long-context): 10 QPS, 80% requests with 2048 tokens output, intensive KV-cache usage.

Example profile snippet:

---
profile_name: large-gen
qps: 10
sequence_length:
  input: 512
  output: 2048
mix:
  generation: 95
  embeddings: 5
kvs:
  prefix_hit_rate: 0.65
  kv_ops_per_request: 2
---

Failure scenarios and injection matrix:

- Network partitions: simulate partial control-plane -> worker plane partitions and assert TLS fallback and routing policies.
- Slow KMS: add 200–1000ms latency to KMS calls and assert request error-rates remain below 0.5% for SLA-backed customers.
- GPU eviction simulation: sequentially drain and taint worker GPU slots and validate tenant failover and graceful degradation.
- KV inconsistency: introduce out-of-order KV-appends to check convergence and correctness of model state after catch-up.
- Model artifact corruption: feed an intentionally truncated model file and validate runtime rejects with clear error and falls back.

Telemetry assertions and acceptance criteria:

The telemetry validator enforces assertions at both service and tenant granularity. Key assertions: 

- Latency SLOs: generation p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 420ms for small-text-search profile; p50 <= 250ms, p95 <= 1200ms for large-gen (these are validation targets, not guaranteed production SLOs).
- Error budget: end-to-end error rate (5xx or explicit runtime rejects) < 0.3% during the validation window.
- Token accounting: per-tenant token counts and cost ledger must match simulated inputs within 0.5%.
- Output fidelity (golden prompts): normalized token-level diff (BLEU-like) <= 2% on curated evaluation set after model swap. Any regression > 2% triggers hold.
- KV consistency: after simulated migration, sample 1000 state keys and assert deterministic values match pre-migration baseline.

Acceptance checklist (automated and manual steps):

Automated gating: 
1. All telemetry assertions are green.
2. Evidence bundle generated and checksum verified.
3. No fatal runtime rejects in error logs.

Manual review gating (operator):
1. Compare golden prompt diffs and confirm no semantic regressions.
2. Verify rollout playbook steps and human approvals are recorded.
3. Sign the CAT (Customer Acceptance Test) artifact when deploying to a customer.

Rollback triggers and automated backout policy:

- Immediate automatic rollback if any of the following are observed during a staged upgrade: crash-looping control-plane node, >1% sustained increase in p99 latency for two consecutive 10-minute windows, or token accounting discrepancy > 1% for billing-critical tenants.
- If rollback triggers, the harness executes these steps:
  1) Quiesce new client connections.
  2) Re-point traffic to previous model binary snapshot or previous container image.
  3) Restore KV snapshot and replay any missing operations.
  4) Re-run golden prompt set and validate parity.
  5) Generate a rollback report and mark run as failed for release dashboard.

Example rollback command sequence (CLI):

# Gracefully mark candidate version as draining
redwoodctl candidate set-drain --version v2026.03-candidate --reason "telemetry-regression"

# Roll traffic back to previous stable image
redwoodctl rollout promote --from v2026.02-stable --to production --force --note "auto-rollback"

Evidence bundle and audit artifacts:

The harness produces a bundle in S3-compatible storage (or local object store for air-gapped runs). Bundle contents:
- logs/ (structured logs from controller, generators, runtime)
- traces/ (Jaeger trace captures around failures)
- metrics/ (Prometheus scrape dumps)
- golden-diffs/ (per-prompt diffs and similarity scores)
- kv-checksums.csv (sampled pre/post migration)
- run-report.json (summary metadata, pass/fail flags, checklist status)

The run-report is machine-readable for the release pipeline; a human-friendly SUMMARY.txt is also included.

Sanitization and customer data handling:

- Use only sanitized exports from production. Replace PII using redaction toolchain (script: scripts/sanitize-export.sh).
- Generate synthetic tenant identifiers. Do not run with customer KMS keys; use test keys or HSM simulator.

Packaging and CI integration:

- The harness is shipped as a Helm chart (chart/harness/) and a CLI artifact (bin/validation-runner). CI job definitions (Jenkins / GitHub Actions) live under infra/pipelines/validate-upgrades.yaml.
- Typical pipeline steps: build artifacts -> create validation cluster -> deploy harness -> run suite -> collect evidence -> mark release pass/fail.

Runbook (step-by-step):

1) Prepare: ensure sanitized KV snapshot is uploaded and candidate images are available.
2) Bootstrap cluster: helm install harness --values ci/values-qa.yaml
3) Start profile: validation-runner start --profile large-gen --duration 60m --evidence-bucket s3://redwood-validation/runs/2026-03-01-abc
4) Monitor: tail logs and telemetry dashboard; the telemetry validator posts status to /status endpoint.
5) On success: download evidence bundle, attach to release ticket, notify release owner for manual review.
6) On failure: trigger automated rollback, collect post-rollback evidence, and open incident if regressions persist.

Operational ownership and SLAs for validation runs:

- Owner: eng-private-deployments upgrade team. Primary on-call: @upgrade-squad (rotating).
- Target run time for a standard validation (1 hour profile): full run + evidence packaging completes in <= 120 minutes. If packaging takes longer, pipeline marks run degraded.

Metrics the team dashboards should include:

- Run success rate (7d/30d)
- Median evidence bundle creation time
- Average validation runtime per profile
- Number of auto-rollbacks triggered and root-cause categories

Known limitations and future work:

- The harness currently simulates GPU thermal events through throttling rather than physical power cycling; we plan to integrate with rack-level testbeds for hardware-induced faults in 2026 Q3.
- Long-duration soak tests and regulatory customer-specific CAR tests are executed in separate labs (link to scheduling page required).

Appendices:

A. Example golden prompt verification script (bash):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for f in golden-prompts/*.jsonl; do
  jq -c . $f | while read -r j; do
    prompt=$(echo "$j" | jq -r .prompt)
    expected=$(echo "$j" | jq -r .expected)
    got=$(curl -sS -X POST https://runtime.test.local/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer test" -d "{\"prompt\":\"$prompt\"}")
    sim=$(python3 tools/token_similarity.py --expected "$expected" --actual "$got")
    echo "$f,$sim" >> results.csv
  done
done

B. Sample profile directory layout:

/profiles/
  large-gen.yaml
  conversational-saas.yaml
  small-text-search.yaml
